newsitem.title: MEXICO: INVESTORS SET TO SURF MEXICAN WAVE OF STATISTICS.
newsitem.headline: INVESTORS SET TO SURF MEXICAN WAVE OF STATISTICS.

text.p: A Mexican wave of statistics due out over the coming week looks likely to give investors the ride they want, as Mexico's recovery rolls on, economists say.

Second quarter gross domestic product (GDP) is slated for release next Tuesday, but economists say industrial production data scheduled for publication on Thursday will give a good idea of how that key number will look.
Before that GDP number is released, however, Mexico's Finance Ministry is expected to publish its second quarter statement of public finances on Friday.
Analysts are widely predicting a surplus that is likely to be the last quarter in the black for some time.

"The GDP figure is definitely more important than the government's fiscal accounts," said Enrique Ramirez, economist at Santander Investment. "Economists will be waiting for June industrial production and most will revise their (GDP) forecasts after that figure."
A Reuter survey of 13 Mexico City-based analysts, published on Monday, showed an average forecast for June industrial production of a rise of 8.30 percent after May's 9.0 percent.

But as Mexico's recovery broadens out from its export base to include a revival in consumption, some economists are feeling much more bullish. J.P. Morgan's Alfredo Thorne is going for an increase in industrial production of 11.3 percent in June and 11.8 percent for the quarter, based on revitalized consumer demand and a pickup in manufacturing -- as already seen in June trade balance data.
